language_wrapper: Consider the equation x^{ {m} } - {m} x^{ {m}-1 } + C({m},2) x^{ {m}-2 } - C({m},3) x^{ {m}-3 } + ... + (-1)^{ {m}-1 } C({m},{m}-1) x = {t}. Let P be the product of all nonreal roots of this equation. Compute floor(P).
hardness_rationale: The seed quartic disguises (x−1)^4−1=t and uses the i and −i roots to compute the product of nonreal roots. Our family generalizes to degree m≥6 with alternating binomial coefficients, requiring recognition of (x−1)^m−1=t, handling parity (odd m having one real root; even m having two real roots), and using the m-th roots of unity product identity ∏(z−rζ)=z^m−r^m to extract the product over subsets of roots. The solver must divide by the product of real roots to isolate the nonreal part, deriving explicit formulas P=(t+2)/(1+r) for odd m and P=t/(r^2−1) for even m. This demands deeper algebraic insight and number theory (roots of unity and Vieta-like products) than the original, and cannot be solved by simple numeric guessing.
notes: Proof outline: Write the given polynomial as (x−1)^m−1=t, so (x−1)^m=t+1. Let r=(t+1)^{1/m} and let ζ range over the m-th roots of unity. The roots are x_j=1+rζ_j. Using the identity ∏_{j=0}^{m−1}(z−rζ_j)=z^m−r^m, set z=−1 and multiply by (−1)^m to obtain ∏_{j}(1+rζ_j)=1−(−1)^m r^m=1−(−1)^m(t+1). For odd m, the only real root is x=1+r; hence the product of nonreal roots is (t+2)/(1+r). For even m, the real roots are x=1±r, whose product is 1−r^2; hence the product of nonreal roots is [1−(t+1)]/(1−r^2)=t/(r^2−1). Both expressions are positive reals. The floor is then computed from these formulas. The generator enforces nontriviality and avoids borderline floors to ensure robustness.
source_question: Let $P$ be the product of the nonreal roots of $x^4-4x^3+6x^2-4x=2005.$ Find $\lfloor P\rfloor.$
